summary: To ship OAuth for Notion, the developer must create an internal connection in the Notion Developer portal, convert it to a public connection by setting an installation scope and redirect URIs, and then implement the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow to exchange temporary codes for access tokens.
difficulty_reason: Creating a public connection is self-serve via the Developer portal and requires no initial platform review to obtain OAuth credentials or begin testing with users.
approval_wait: 5-10 business days (only if submitting to the Marketplace)
approval_details: Review by the Notion team is only required if you choose to submit your public connection to the Notion Marketplace. Otherwise, basic OAuth usage requires no approval.

requirements.text: Workspace owner permissions are required to create integrations and access the Connections tab.

evidence.quote: Only Workspace owners will be able to access the Connections tab and create integrations.

steps.text: Navigate to Notion, open Settings from your left sidebar, navigate to the Connections tab, and turn on Developer Mode.

evidence.quote: In your left sidebar, navigate to Settings and then the Connections tab... Turn on Developer Mode, then open personal access tokens from the developer section in your sidebar.

steps.title: Log in and turn on Developer Mode

steps.text: Click + New connection, provide a Name, optionally upload a Logo, and select your Associated workspace.

evidence.quote: Click + New connection. Provide a Name for your connection. Optionally, you can also upload an image to use as a Logo. Use the dropdown menu to specify which Associated workspace...

steps.title: Create an internal connection

steps.text: Navigate to the Developer portal under Public connections, configure redirect URI(s), and select your installation scope (Either 'Any workspace' or 'Selected workspaces only').

evidence.quote: In the Build section of the sidebar, select Public connections... Click Create new connection and fill in the required fields, including: Connection name and development workspace, Redirect URI(s)... Installation scope...

steps.title: Convert to a public connection and set installation scope

steps.text: Visit the Configuration tab of your newly created public connection to retrieve your OAuth client ID and client secret.

evidence.quote: After creation, visit the Configuration tab to retrieve your OAuth client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Retrieve OAuth credentials

steps.text: Construct a link to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize with parameters client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, and owner=user, and have users visit it to grant workspace access.

evidence.quote: The URL begins with https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize and has the following parameters: client_id, redirect_uri, response_type, owner...

steps.title: Direct users to the authorization URL

steps.text: Retrieve the temporary code parameter from your redirect URI and make a POST request to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token using HTTP Basic Authentication with your encoded client ID and secret, passing grant_type='authorization_code', code, and redirect_uri in the JSON body.

evidence.quote: send the code as part of a POST request to Notion’s token endpoint: https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token.

steps.title: Exchange authorization code for an access token

steps.text: Go to the Marketplace listing dashboard, select Connections under Drafts, fill in your listing information, and submit it for review.

evidence.quote: In the Listings section of the sidebar, select Connections. Under Drafts, click Start a new connection listing... Submit your listing for review by the Notion team.

steps.title: Submit listing to the Marketplace (Optional)

nuances.text: Installation scope (Any workspace vs. Selected workspaces only) is set once at creation time and cannot be changed afterward.

evidence.quote: Installation scope is set once, at creation time, and can’t be changed afterward. If you pick Selected workspaces only and later want to list on the Marketplace, create a new connection.

nuances.text: Unlike internal connections, public connections require each individual member of a workspace to complete the OAuth flow separately if they want to use it.

evidence.quote: Unlike internal connections, if multiple members in a workspace want to use a public connection, each prospective user needs to individually follow the auth flow for the connection.

blockers.issue: Connection fails with access or content errors during use
blockers.why_it_happens: The user may not have authenticated with the proper account, or the page was not shared via the page picker.
blockers.workaround: Confirm the user authenticated with the correct account or re-authenticate through connection settings.

evidence.quote: You may not have authenticated with the account that has access. You can connect multiple accounts either through Settings → My connections, or the error drop down.

agent_can_do: Handle the OAuth token exchange POST request
Call Notion API endpoints using the acquired access tokens
developer_must_do: Log in as a workspace owner and turn on Developer Mode
Create and configure the public connection in the developer portal
Store client IDs and secrets securely as environment variables
unverified: Exact token expiration lifetimes in seconds/milliseconds for public OAuth access tokens.
Whether refresh tokens are issued and what their lifetime policy is.
